premise.claim: CacheRuntime: a partially specified `resources` silently drops the rest of the container's resource requirements (issue #6173): setting just limits.memory clears requests.cpu, limits.cpu, requests.memory and claims on the next reconcile.
premise.evidence: On merge-base e0fc4c1 the three contract tests fail with requests.cpu="0", requests.memory="0", limits.cpu="0" (values dropped), exactly the reported symptom; on the PR head they pass. See results/unit-base.txt vs results/unit-head.txt.

findings.note: Contract intentionally redefined by the PR at ecd41afa (head e259d738): the #6165-era 'neither side declares -> workload untouched' guard was replaced by 'cleared'. Old guard removed; this pins the new contract. RED on base e0fc4c1 and previous head c1c303e8, GREEN on e259d738.
Guard added round 2: drifted workload + template-only config is restored to the template and converges. GREEN on base, previous head and head.

Round-2 canary (zz_adhoc_f6_test.go, never committed) reproduced F6 on e259d738; the head fix f02054bd inverts it into these contract tests. RED on base e0fc4c18 and previous head e259d738, GREEN on 497bbeaf. Compile-safe on all three refs (pre-existing symbols only).

Sync path must refuse a conflicting merge: workload resources untouched, Warning event RuntimeResourcesConflict naming the key, nil error, convergent. RED on base and previous head, GREEN on 497bbeaf.

FIXED at head 3adc547d: validateResourceRequirements now mirrors the apiserver rule for non-overcommittable resources (hugepages-*, extended) -- request must equal limit, and a request needs a limit -- via a local isOvercommitAllowed mirror (the k8s.io/kubernetes helper package is genuinely not vendored; verified byte-equivalent logic against v1.29.15 helpers.go:127 + validation.go:6568-6579). Both contract tests flip RED->GREEN exactly at 3adc547d: RED on base e0fc4c18 and previous head 497bbeaf (invalid pair applied silently), GREEN on head (workload untouched, Warning event naming the key). The additive second test pins the request-without-limit sub-rule. The F9 remedy's third element (hugepages-require-cpu-or-memory cross-key check) was consciously scoped out by the author; adjudicated sound: merge is key-union per list, so a presence violation needs an already-invalid input, and no layer pod-validates the CRs -- a pre-existing gap outside the merge-synthesized class.

FIXED at head a773dfa6 (round-6 remedy): validDesiredResources drops a container claim the workload's pod spec neither declares nor already carries, emits a RuntimeResourcesConflict Warning naming the claim, and still syncs the rest of resources (splitDeclaredClaims, transform_common.go). Round-4 canary retired: it was observed FLIPPED at head (log line 'CANARY FLIPPED: the template's container claim no longer propagates') but its log-and-return shape could never report the flip as a failure -- inverted into these contract tests per the polarity rule. Differential cells: test 1 RED on base e0fc4c18 (claim silently absent under wholesale apply, no warning) and previous head ce4f0c4f (claim propagated, no warning), GREEN at head; tests 2-3 are pass-through pins green on every ref (no over-block, no spurious roll). Creation-side gap (CacheRuntime claim undeclared by the template) remains a documented limitation, unchanged by this remedy.

Round-5 remedy 94121e27: syncRuntimeSpec returns nil for a class without a topology instead of panicking at runtimeClass.Topology.Master. Pre-existing gap (getRuntimeClass rejects such classes before syncRuntimeSpec in production; the guard protects direct callers). The test recovers the panic into a clean failure. RED on base e0fc4c18 and previous head 3adc547d (nil-pointer deref), GREEN at head ce4f0c4f (nil error, master and worker workloads untouched).

Round-5 remedy 71d94397 (+4a8668f9 pinning event count): the creation path now emits exactly one Warning event with the specific RuntimeResourcesConflict reason (naming the conflict) when the merged resources are rejected, for worker, master and client -- on top of the reconciler's generic ErrorProcessRuntime. RED on base e0fc4c18 (no validation, no error) and previous head 3adc547d (error without any event), GREEN at head ce4f0c4f. Client variant closes the last component without a creation-rejection spec.
